indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the word for a show, splitting it open

parts.note: a parade is a public show or procession
one is I, and one's stands for one is, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: A performance takes place up in the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: Show looks like a verb, but it is the noun; one's must be read as one is, and in signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a synonym for the blissful afterlife of the blessed.

explanation.surface: A slogan for transparency in the running of the state.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one political phrase, but each separately defines the answer: one as an adjective meaning not secret, the other as the adjective for state matters, as in public spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open is available to all people, and the same adjective describes affairs of the state, as in office or spending run by the state.

parts.note: bloody meat, such as steak barely cooked, is rare
a good man is a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Praise for an exceptionally fine fellow, with a British expletive thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloody looks like British emphasis, but it is a steak barely cooked; good man is the crossword convention for a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something most uncommon or exceptional is a superlative of scarcity.

clue.text: Died before time at great cost

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in family trees
something done before its time is early

explanation.surface: Someone died young, and it was a heavy loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay for something heavily, with much sacrifice, is to pay a high price for it.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the two words might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Chapped, sore lips in cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Perhaps turns LIPS and TENDER into a new arrangement of ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood that has split into sharp fragments has cracked.

explanation.surface: Two words that summon up an arid landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert looks like a noun beside sands, but it is the verb meaning abandon; sands is the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone in a helpless spot is to leave them stuck, and a shore or beach is an old word for the seaside.

parts.note: to rip is to tear
off, as in gone off, means away

explanation.surface: Someone yanks a hooded sweatshirt off a person.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoodie looks like the garment, but in Britain it also means a young hooligan wearing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, unruly young person, a hooligan, is the kind of youth the hooded-top label is applied to.

parts.note: to state an opinion is to air it, so states means airs
a holiday away is a trip

explanation.surface: A trip to America starts at this place, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: States looks like the USA, but it is the verb airs; the whole clue also describes a landing strip where a flying holiday starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway for aircraft is where a flight, and so a trip abroad, gets under way.

indicators.note: taking means the word for a performance takes in, holds, the other piece

parts.note: a performance or act carried out is a deed
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: Someone loathed sitting a test as part of an act.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is to abhor it.

parts.note: in the main means at sea, where a shellfish clinging to a hull or rock cannot be dislodged; the surface reads as mostly unshakeable

explanation.walkthrough: In the main looks like the phrase meaning generally, but the main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean clings fast to ships and rocks in the sea and is famously hard to dislodge.

parts.note: par is the standard, as in up to par
rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Say once more that the usual stuff is junk.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo words mechanically, without understanding, is what a talking bird does.

indicators.note: broadcast, like seed scattered widely, tells us the letters are scattered and reset

parts.note: the name Elton with its S

explanation.surface: Elton John goes on air and turns rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast shuffles ELTONS plus IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude, disrespectful, offensive behaviour is cheeky and rude.

parts.note: a male person is a man

indicators.note: chewed up suggests the word is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A male creature gets eaten, as happens to some insects after mating.
explanation.walkthrough: Chewed up gives TIS; the 's of Insect's is a link meaning is. The female of this insect famously eats the male, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying insect of that name is a predatory bug with folded forelegs.

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of the following words are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Digging out a mineral that turns into a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning rearranges OUT plus MINERAL; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a crystalline silicate mineral cut as a precious stone in many colours.

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild treatment, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor confesses to hamming it up shamelessly to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: Outrageously rearranges I plus OVERACTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornamental serves to look good rather than for use.

parts.note: interest here is money charged on a loan, so taking a great deal of it describes a loan shark, not curiosity

explanation.walkthrough: Taking great interest looks like being very curious, but interest is the charge on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lending money at exorbitant rates of charge is the classic sense of extortionate lending.

indicators.note: holding means the word for a non-believer holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a heretic holds beliefs against church doctrine
M is the standard abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: An unbeliever attends a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks like the church service, but it is M from physics.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal that is airtight is completely sealed shut.

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A diet followed constantly makes someone slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delicate, light and airy, almost insubstantial, is flimsy.

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, signalling rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A thespian is wanted in the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Fancy rearranges THEATRES plus WE. Luvvie is British slang for a gushing actor, and also a term of endearment like love.
explanation.definitionFit: Luvvie is a British endearment, a variant of love, used to a darling.

indicators.note: before places the odds ahead of the word for study

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the final betting odds when a race begins
to study a subject at university is to read it

explanation.surface: A punter checks the last betting prices before the race is televised.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is British horse-racing jargon; to read a subject is British for studying it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To disseminate news widely is to circulate it.

indicators.note: covered in means the gangster is wrapped inside the word for blood

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster, giving AL

explanation.surface: A mobster is drenched in blood all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in abundance, aplenty, can be found all around.

indicators.note: in places the church abbreviation inside the word for split

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A modern church divided by schism.
explanation.walkthrough: Latter-day suggests the Mormon church, but here it just means modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of modern times belongs to a period not long past.

clue.text: Conned a politician taken by socialist

indicators.note: taken by means the socialist takes the other pieces into itself

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist or communist
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A left-winger takes in a gullible MP.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramp is British slang for a swindle, so ramped means swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, a ramp is a swindle or racket, so to have been ramped is to have been cheated.

indicators.note: following puts the trail after the twist

parts.note: to warp is to twist out of shape
a lane is a narrow path or trail

explanation.surface: A vapour trail twisting behind a wartime fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spitfire was a famous British fighter aircraft of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spitfire is an example: a fighter aircraft built for combat.

explanation.surface: Someone launching a new store.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening looks like the act of opening a shop, but it is a noun, a vent; the other sense is a retail store.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent or exit for water or gas is an aperture, and a retail store selling goods is a point of sale.

indicators.note: about means the book goes round the word for anger

parts.note: a tome is a large book
ire is anger, and anger's adds the S

explanation.surface: A book about rage that is a dull read.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious and wearisome makes you weary.

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ickle is British baby talk for little

explanation.surface: A tiny little implement.
explanation.walkthrough: Ickle is British nursery slang for little.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved blade on a handle is a farm hand implement for cutting crops.

clue.text: Most exciting and wilts in passion!

indicators.note: in places the word for wilts inside the word for passion

parts.note: heat means passion, as in the heat of the moment
a plant that wilts dies

explanation.surface: Thrills, with someone flagging in the heat of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Headiest is the superlative of heady: intoxicating, most thrilling.
